messages:
Asha: heads up — p95 on /rerank-embed spiked after the seq_cutoff tuner we flipped this morning :grimacing:
Sam: ok what's the delta?
Asha: quick snapshot:
- QPS stable ~310
- p50 ~52ms, p95 moved 190ms -> 480ms
- median batch occupancy fell 14 -> 6
- global kv_cache.hit_rate 80% -> 52%
- kernel_fallback_rate ~22% (mostly seq>1100 path)
Liu: ugh. can you paste traces or prom queries you used?
Asha: yep, here's what we ran in grafana:
```
sum(rate(rerank.requests_total[1m])) by (route)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(rerank.latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,route))
sum by (kernel_reason) (rate(inf.kernel_choice_total[5m]))
sum by (batch_bucket) (rate(inf.batch.kv_hit_total[1m]))
```
Asha: flamegraph notes: hot path moves into custom_attention_long when seq > cutoff; prefix recompute spikes correlate with low kv_hits
Nate: did anything else change? batching tunables, autoscale, or traffic shape?
Asha: only two changes: seq_cutoff threshold lowered (to prefer newer kernel for shorter seqs) and min_batch_delay increased 2ms->7ms as an experiment to try to improve throughput on other routes
Sam: increasing delay should normally increase batch sizes; but if traffic is bursty we can get worse occupancies and more sequences hitting the long-path kernel -> fallback hot spot
Liu: so KV hit drop is likely secondary to smaller coalesced prefixes. We need per-batch kv_hit to see the distribution. Current metric is coarse minute-level aggregate
Asha: propose dashboard updates:
- heatmap: route x batch_size_bucket showing kv_hit_ratio (buckets: 1,2-3,4-7,8-15,16+)
- stacked token-latency panel: color by kernel_reason and split by kv_hit boolean (hit/miss) at p50/p95
- batch occupancy histogram + moving median line
- kernel_fallback_rate timeseries per route (annotate seq_cutoff flips)
Sam: tracing: temporarily bump rerank trace sampling from 0.5% -> 4% while p95 > 350ms for a 20m window. Make it a runtime toggle so ops can flip quickly
Asha: pseudo-alert rule I sketched:
```
if histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(rerank.latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) > 0.35:
  runtime.set("trace.sample.rerank", 0.04)
else:
  runtime.set("trace.sample.rerank", 0.005)
```
Liu: add labels to traces: kernel_reason=(seq_cutoff|quant_miss|fallback) and batch_id; include batch_size tag for correlating cache usage
Nate: operationally how fast can we revert the seq_cutoff change? is it a deploy or a runtime flag?
Asha: it's behind a feature-gate runtime flag we can flip per-canary. also adding an auto-revert rule: if kernel_fallback_rate > 12% AND p95 delta > 200ms for 5m -> revert to previous cutoff
deploy-bot: auto-revert executed for canary at 1853071500 — feature_gate.seq_cutoff restored to previous value :white_check_mark:
Asha: after the canary revert p95 in that cohort trended back down within ~4 minutes; global rollback pending review
Liu: for panels I'll implement:
- kernel_vs_batch heatmap with kv_hit overlay and per-cell counts
- small panel: kv_hit_ratio_by_batch_bucket (timeseries)
- single-number alert: kv_hit drop > 15% vs 7d baseline for rerank routes
- kernel_fallback_rate alert > 10% sustained for 5m
Sam: good. also add an experiment to restore min_batch_delay -> 2ms in a small cohort to measure occupancy and kv hits; run for 45m and report
Asha: will schedule the min_batch_delay revert experiment at 1853072100 and capture batch occupancy + kv_trace samples
Nate: once you have dashboards PR and runtime flag PR, tag ops and me. keep change windows short and prefer automated revert thresholds
Asha: will open grafana PR and runtime flag PR in #eng-runtime, include screenshots and prom snippets. posting perf diffs and flamegraphs shortly :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Sam: thanks — prioritize quick rollback path and clear alerts. ping when PRs are up :thumbsup:
